S1_Title: Anemia — one of the most common findings in medicine, and one of the most misunderstood. A sign, not a diagnosis.
S2_Oxygen: Why does low hemoglobin matter? Red blood cells carry hemoglobin, and each hemoglobin molecule carries oxygen. So when hemoglobin falls, less oxygen reaches the tissues — and that gap is what produces every symptom of anemia.
S3_Definition: So what counts as anemia? By W-H-O criteria, hemoglobin below thirteen grams per deciliter in men, below twelve in non-pregnant women, and below eleven in pregnancy — though thresholds vary with age and altitude.
S4_Mechanisms: There are only two ways to get there. Either the marrow makes less — iron deficiency, B-twelve or folate deficiency, marrow failure, or chronic disease — or red cells are lost or destroyed faster. Same endpoint — different workup.
S5_MCV: The practical first step is the M-C-V: the size of the red cell. Small cells suggest iron deficiency, thalassemia, or chronic disease. Normal cells: acute blood loss, kidney disease, or early iron deficiency. Large cells: B-twelve or folate deficiency, liver disease, or hypothyroidism. Follow-up testing is guided by the column.
S6_Close: Patients present with fatigue, pallor, breathlessness on exertion, dizziness, and tachycardia. But remember: anemia is a clue, not an answer. Treat the cause — not just the number.
